title: The Trinity
lead: The Christian teaching that the one God exists as three Persons, Father, Son and Holy Spirit, equal and eternal. The word is not in the Bible; the doctrine was set out at the councils of Nicaea (325) and Constantinople (381) from texts such as Matthew 28:19, John 1, John 14–17 and Paul's letters, which speak of Father, Son and Spirit together. Jews and Muslims, and some groups that call themselves Christian, reject it as incompatible with the oneness of God.

sections.h: Father, Son and Spirit in the New Testament
sections.b: The New Testament keeps Israel's confession that God is one (Mark 12:29; 1 Corinthians 8:6) while naming Father, Son and Spirit together in baptism (Matthew 28:19), in blessing (2 Corinthians 13:14) and in the life of the church (1 Corinthians 12:4–6). John's farewell discourse is a central source: the Son is in the Father and the Father in him (John 14:10), the Father sends the Spirit in the Son's name (John 14:26), and the Spirit comes out from the Father (John 15:26). Later councils turned these patterns into the doctrine of one being in three Persons.
